World.title: Nortje returns to boost Blitzboks’ strike power at World Champs in Hong Kong
World.content:
Quewin Nortje returns to the Springbok Sevens squad for the HSBC SVNS World Championship opener in Hong Kong next weekend.

The 23-year-old missed all six regular HSBC SVNS Series stops due to injury this season. Nortje last featured at the inaugural World Championship tournament in Los Angeles in May 2025. The Blitzboks won that title, and now they target more silverware in the Far East.

“Someone like Quewin worked very hard over a couple of months in that role and now will be ready to contribute as we know he can,” head coach Philip Snyman said.



INJURY CASUALTIES OPEN DOOR FOR RETURNING STARS

Three squad changes follow the North American leg, where the Blitzboks won in both Vancouver and New York. Christie Grobbelaar, Dewald Human and Gino Cupido all picked up injuries and cannot travel to Hong Kong.

Zain Davids and Jayden Nell come into the squad to fill the gaps left behind. Davids sat out the North American leg, while Nell impressed on debut in New York last month.

Nell and David Brits will both experience Hong Kong’s famous rugby sevens tournament for the first time. The rest of the squad brings 38 combined visits to the celebrated Kai Tak Sports Park event.

Nortje carries a remarkable strike rate of 32 tries across just 12 tournaments. His return adds serious attacking threat to a side that has won three tournaments in a row.

SNYMAN CALLS FOR FRESH START AHEAD OF WORLD CHAMPIONSHIP BID

Snyman says the team reset completely after returning from North America to Stellenbosch.

“We started over; this is a new challenge and we have some players coming back,” said Snyman. “We had to align first, and the best way to do that is to start at the basics.”



He added the squad pushed each other hard in training ahead of the Hong Kong trip.

The Blitzboks boss explained the team’s focus on Hong Kong began long before this week.

“Doing well in Hong Kong was one of our objectives at the start of this campaign. Nothing has changed from our competitive excellence mindset in camp.”

The coach confirmed the squad travels with strong belief in their ability to perform on the big stage.

BLITZBOKS’ POOL A SCHEDULE

The Springbok Sevens side landed in Pool A alongside Argentina, Spain and Uruguay at Kai Tak Sports Park.

The Blitzboks open their campaign against Uruguay on Friday, 17 April, at 05h16 SA time. They then face Spain at 08h49 before taking on Argentina on Saturday morning at 06h13. All matches are broadcast live on SuperSport.

The squad departs for Hong Kong on Thursday. Hong Kong remains the only HSBC SVNS venue here the Blitzboks have not yet won a title.

Springbok Sevens squad for Hong Kong: Ryan Oosthuizen, Impi Visser (captain), Zain Davids, Ronald Brown, Selvyn Davids, Siviwe Soyizwapi, Shilton van Wyk, Quewin Nortje, Donavan Don, Sebastiaan Jobb, David Brits, Tristan Leyds, Jayden Nell.

World.title: Tyla embraces her Zulu roots
World.content:
Tyla embraced her South African Zulu roots through a sentimental fashion token from her beloved grandmother.



In honour of her grandmother’s birthday, which was on Sunday, 5 April, Tyla shared a photo of herself wearing a traditional Zulu beaded necklace known as ubuhlalu in isiZulu.

TYLA’S GRANDMOTHER HANDMADE BEADED NECKLACE

Tyla styled her beaded necklace with ripped jeans, and her poses perfectly showcased the necklace’s beauty in what seemed like a music video for an upcoming project.

Her caption summed up her love and appreciation for the necklace and her dearest grandmother.

“My gran handmade this and reminds me every time I visit that I BETTA [better] post her piece HBD [happy birthday, gran] gran,” wrote Tyla.

TYLA: ‘THE SWEETEST SOUL’

In September 2025, the Grammy winner mourned the loss of her grandmother.



She fondly remembered her grandmother for sharing her Zulu heritage, which also encompassed her Indian, Irish, Mauritian, and Coloured background.

She described her late grandmother as “the sweetest soul” and expressed gratitude for “making me the artist I am today.”

“I thank God for your presence in my life. Thank you for all the love and all the stories you would tell me. Your presence will forever be missed. The sweetest soul,” wrote Tyla.

“You were always proud of your mother and called us royalty because of her. Thank you for teaching me about my Zulu heritage and making me the artist I am today,” she added.

“Your presence will forever be missed. The sweetest soul. I love you, Gran,” she concluded.

TYLA COOKED A PROUDLY MZANSI MEAL FOR VOGUE

Embracing her South African roots appears to be like a badge of honour for Tyla.



In the March 2025 edition of British Vogue, she cooked a classic South African dish that included pap, chutney, and boerewors.

Below are some of her most memorable quotes from the cooking video:

“I’m not the best cook, [but] I can cook to survive.“

“I picked this because it’s like my favourite food to eat, honestly. I always speak about it, and people don’t know what I mean when I say pap and chutney. They’re like what is that?”

“I love food, but I just don’t like cooking it. I can make you some stuff, but don’t expect every night a whole three-course meal. I’m not like Nara Smith, I promise.”

“This is what I like about pap, like if you feel like it’s going wrong, there’s always a way to fix it. When I was in New York, I made it, I craved it.”



“The spice that I use for the chutney is Robinson’s barbecue spice. This is the best spice, guys. You can use this for everything, like marinade [marinading] your meat, chutney, or food like anything.“

World.title: How South Africa’s 8 billionaires made their money
World.content:
South Africa’s eight wealthiest individuals and families have a combined net worth of an estimated $42.4 billion (about R694 billion). Image: Forbes Africa

South Africa’s eight wealthiest individuals and families have a combined net worth of an estimated $42.4 billion (about R694 billion), according to the latest data from the Forbes Real-Time Billionaires List.

The ranking tracks the fortunes of the world’s richest individuals using share prices, exchange rates and publicly available financial information.

The latest figures show little movement at the top of South Africa’s rich list since the beginning of the year, although some shifts have taken place further down the rankings.



Johan Rupert remains South Africa’s richest

Luxury goods tycoon Johann Rupert retains his position as South Africa’s wealthiest individual.

Rupert, 75, is the chairman of Richemont, the global luxury group behind brands such as Cartier and Montblanc.

He is followed in second place by former diamond magnate Nicky Oppenheimer, 80, whose fortune stems largely from his family’s historic ties to the global diamond industry through De Beers.

Changes within the top five

The remainder of the top five has seen some movement in recent weeks.

Mining entrepreneur Patrice Motsepe – the youngest of South Africa’s billionaires at 64 – has climbed to third place, overtaking media and technology investor Koos Bekker, 73, who now sits in fourth position.

Bekker is best known for transforming Naspers into a global technology investor.



Rounding out the top five is Michiel le Roux, 76, the founder of Capitec Bank, which has grown into one of South Africa’s largest retail banks.

Shifts further down the list

Further down the rankings, retail magnate Christo Wiese, 84, slipped from sixth to seventh place, overtaken by financial services billionaire Jannie Mouton, 79, founder of the investment group PSG Group.

Completing the list is Paul van Zuydam, 88, the South African-born entrepreneur behind the premium cookware brand Le Creuset.

Wealth resilience despite economic pressures

Despite ongoing economic challenges both in South Africa and globally, the fortunes of the country’s wealthiest individuals highlight the continued international reach and resilience of South African business leaders.

Many of the fortunes represented on the list are tied to multinational companies and global markets, insulating them to some extent from local economic volatility.

World’s Richest Person

On the global stage, 54-year-old South Africa-born Elon Musk continues to top the Forbes rankings as the world’s richest person, with a reported net worth of $801.3 billion.

Below, the list of the top eight richest South Africans in the world as of 8 April 2026.

World.title: Tourist fined for exiting vehicle at Kruger National Park in viral video – WATCH
World.content:
A visitor to the Kruger National Park has sparked widespread outrage after being filmed outside his vehicle, breaking park safety rules. Image: Kruger National Park

A visitor to the Kruger National Park has sparked widespread outrage after being filmed outside his vehicle – and reacting angrily – breaking park safety rules.

The incident, which was captured on video and shared on the popular wildlife page Wildest Kruger Sightings this week, quickly went viral, drawing thousands of comments from social media users who criticised the man’s behaviour and called for stricter action.

Tourist fined for leaving vehicle

the page, the man exited his vehicle in an apparent attempt to get a better view of lions.



However, visitors are strictly prohibited from leaving their vehicles in most areas of the park due to the risks posed by wild animals.

Rangers issued the tourist with a R2 500 fine for violating park regulations.

Video footage from the scene shows several vehicles stopped along the road, including a game drive vehicle carrying passengers.

The visibly upset tourist can be seen standing among the vehicles while arguing with a ranger.

At one point, he raises his middle finger (repeatedly) and directs vulgar language at the ranger, who is heard speaking on a walkie-talkie while reportedly alerting park gates to the vehicle’s registration details.

Safety rules in place for visitors and wildlife

The Kruger National Park enforces strict safety rules requiring visitors to remain inside their vehicles in most areas of the reserve.



These regulations are designed to protect both visitors and wildlife, as approaching or provoking animals can lead to dangerous encounters and may result in animals being harmed if they attack a person.

Social media users react

The video quickly attracted strong reactions online, with many users criticising the man’s behaviour and calling for him to face further consequences.

Several users also pointed out that if the man had been attacked by a lion, park authorities may have been forced to euthanise the animal, despite it acting in self-defence.

Here are some of the reactions shared on X:

@SafariWatchSA: “Ban him from every national park. The rules exist for a reason. If a lion attacked him, the animal would have paid the price.”

@BushveldExplorer: “People think wildlife parks are zoos. This is exactly how tragedies happen.”

@EcoGuardZA: “Getting out of your car near lions is not bravery – it’s reckless and selfish.”

@TravelWithLindi: “The ranger was doing his job. The attitude from that tourist is embarrassing.”

Others suggested the man believed he would have time to run back to his vehicle if he spotted a lion, highlighting how dangerous such assumptions can be in a wildlife reserve.

The incident has reignited debate about visitor behaviour in protected areas, with many calling for stronger enforcement of park rules to ensure the safety of both people and wildlife.

World.title: How many doses of breakthrough HIV prevention jab have arrived in SA?
World.content:
The injection is 'preventive medicine,' not a vaccine, and is taken twice a year. Image: WHO

South Africa has received its first shipment of Lenacapavir, a new injectable HIV prevention medicine expected to expand protection options for vulnerable groups.



The Department of Health confirmed that 37 920 doses of the drug arrived in the country last week.

Lenacapavir is a six-monthly injectable designed to prevent HIV infection. Officials say it offers a new option for people who face barriers to existing prevention methods.

The Department said the medicine forms part of integrated and people-centred HIV prevention services.

Health Minister Dr Aaron Motsoaledi welcomed the development.

New HIV prevention option arrives

Lenacapavir is considered one of the most significant HIV prevention advances in recent years.

The injection is preventive medicine, not a vaccine, and is taken twice a year.



It is expected to improve adherence among priority groups, including adolescent girls and young women, sex workers, and gay men.

Officials believe the medicine could help reduce new infections.

The Department said the arrival of Lenacapavir will strengthen efforts to end AIDS as a public health threat by 2030.

Rollout plans to follow

Government will soon announce an official launch for the new prevention programme.

“The Department will in the next few weeks announce the official launch of this game-changer where the phased implementation plan will be outlined,” the department said.

Motsoaledi is expected to announce the launch date in consultation with President Cyril Ramaphosa.



Authorities say the rollout will form part of South Africa’s broader HIV response aligned with the Global AIDS Strategy for 2026–2030.

World.title: First ships through Strait of Hormuz since ceasefire, but NOT heading to SA
World.content:
Two ships have passed through the Strait of Hormuz since Iran agreed to reopen the waterway as part of a ceasefire deal. Image: Flickr

Two ships have passed through the Strait of Hormuz since Iran agreed to reopen the waterway as part of a ceasefire deal.

This was according to maritime monitor Marine Traffic said on Wednesday.

“The Greek-owned bulk carrier NJ Earth crossed the Strait at 08:44 UTC, while the Liberia-flagged Daytona Beach transited earlier at 06:59 UTC, shortly after departing Bandar Abbas at 05:28 UTC”, MarineTraffic said on X.



‘Too soon to tell’

The United States and Iran agreed overnight from Tuesday to Wednesday to a two-week ceasefire, during which passage through the Strait of Hormuz “will be possible via coordination with Iran’s Armed Forces”, Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on X.

“NJ Earth’s transit may be an early sign of movement, but it is still too soon to tell whether this reflects a broader ceasefire-driven reopening or a previously approved exception”, Ana Subasic, analyst at MarineTraffic owner Kpler told AFP.

The Greek-owned ship kept its transponder signal on as it transited the strait via an Iranian-approved route near Larak Island, used by most vessels crossing the waterway for the past three weeks.

AFP could not immediately confirm the ship’s destination, but they are not heading to South Africa.

Preparing to move vessels

“While we expect more crossings in the coming days, from a risk and compliance perspective this first transit should be read cautiously,” Subasic added.

Some shipowners and charterers are preparing to move their vessels stuck in the Gulf, shipping journal Lloyd’s List reported on Wednesday morning. It estimates around 800 ships are currently stuck in the Gulf.



Access to the strait was severely restricted by Iran in retaliation against US and Israeli attacks since February 28.

From March 1 to April 7, commodities carriers have made 307 crossings, according to Kpler data, a 95-percent decrease from peacetime traffic.

Around a fifth of global crude oil and liquefied natural gas (LNG) passes through the dbwaterway in peacetime.

By Garrin Lambley © Agence France-Presse

World.title: R45m needed to refurbish Riverlea Secondary School after fire
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Gauteng Education Department needs R45-million to refurbish Riverlea Secondary School after it was gutted by a fire just a day before the reopening of the second term.

The fire gutted several classrooms on Tuesday, and it disrupted classes of at least 700 pupils.

READ | Fire erupts again at Riverlea Secondary school ahead of reopening

This is not the first time the school has been engulfed in flames.

A similar incident happened last April, when a fire destroyed classrooms just six days before the start of the term.

At the time, three minors had come forward claiming they had a hand in the fire.

READ | Three 11-year-olds come forward following Riverlea High School fire

During a visit to the school on Wednesday, Gauteng MEC for Education and Sports, Arts, Culture and Recreation, Lebogang Maile revealed another incident that took place in 2007.

This, he said, highlights a disturbing pattern that needs to be addressed. He added that the fire which broke out at the school cannot be justified.

World.title: System being exploited for corruption - TMPD Deputy Commissioner Bolhuis
World.content:
PRETORIA - Tshwane Metro Police Department Deputy Commissioner, Sean Bolhuis said certain elements within the city are exploiting the system for corruption.

He was testifying before the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry on Wednesday.

Bolhuis testified that both he and the chief were used because much of the wrongdoing occurred under their watch.

"We were used as decent, law-abiding, loyal officials, both me, the chief of police, other officials, we were used because it happened under our nose. And it's shameful. We could have done better," he testified.

Wrapping up her testimony earlier, TMPD chief, Yolande Faro, told the Madlanga Commission she only became aware of the appointment of security service provider El Shaddai after the deal had already been signed.

She insisted she had no prior knowledge of any plans to bring the company on board.

Testimony at the Madlanga Commission is raising serious questions about procurement practices and oversight within the TMPD.

World.title: Phala Phala Farm Theft | Judgment expected within a month
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The Constitutional Court of South Africa said judgment in the Phala Phala matter is now at an advanced stage.

The Apex Court said it expects to deliver the ruling within a month.

The case, brought by the Economic Freedom Fighters, challenges the way Parliament handled the scandal involving President Cyril Ramaphosa, including its decision not to proceed with an impeachment process.

READ | Phala-Phala Farm Theft | Robbery trial resumes

At the centre of the saga are allegations linked to the 2020 theft of foreign currency from the President’s Phala Phala farm, as well as questions over whether proper procedures were followed.

The matter was heard in late 2024, but judgment has been reserved for more than a year, well beyond the usual timeframe.

The update comes amid mounting pressure from the EFF, which today staged a march to the court, demanding the release of the long-awaited ruling.

World.title: Suspect remains silent in Swiss bar fire probe
World.content:
CRANS-MONTANA - A former fire safety official in the Swiss ski resort of Crans-Montana remained silent when questioned Wednesday by prosecutors investigating a deadly New Year blaze, his lawyer said.

"My client exercised his right to remain silent as he does not yet have access to the case file," lawyer Fabien Mingard told AFP.

"He will answer the public prosecutors' questions as soon as he has access to the file."

The former head of the Crans-Montana municipality's fire safety department has not been named by Swiss media.

"The hearing lasted only 15-20 minutes because the defendant refused to cooperate after being informed of the charges," Robert Assael, one of the lawyers for the civil parties in the case, told AFP.

"I am shocked that he did not answer the questions when the victims... are only waiting for one thing: the truth," he said.

The blaze at Le Constellation, a bar in the upmarket Alpine resort, broke out in the early hours of January 1 as people celebrated the New Year.

A total of 41 people, most of them teenagers, were killed, and another 115 were injured in the disaster.

Nine people are under criminal investigation in the case.

They include the bar's French owners, husband and wife Jacques and Jessica Moretti, who face charges of manslaughter by negligence, bodily harm by negligence and arson by negligence.

They have twice been questioned at length by public prosecutors and lawyers for the civil parties.

World.title: Iran truce spurs hopes for world economy, but recovery will be rocky
World.content:
TEHRAN - The ceasefire agreed between Iran and the United States should bring some relief to a world economy that has been roiled since the start of hostilities on February 28, even if not all sectors will rebound at the same pace.

- Oil prices -

The ceasefire sent oil prices tumbling, with the main international contracts falling below $100 a barrel.

That should bring relief for retail customers at the pump, where surging petrol prices in recent weeks have forced many countries to take measures to reduce consumption and protect the most vulnerable.

In France, fuel prices could fall by "5 to 10 cents" per litre "very quickly," Olivier Gantois, president of the French Union of Petroleum Industries (Ufip), told AFP.

- Opening of Hormuz -

Two ships, one Greek-owned and the other flying the Liberian flag, have already transited the Strait of Hormuz since Iran agreed to reopen the strategic waterway, through which approximately 20 percent of the world's crude oil and liquefied natural gas normally passes.

But the Strait "remains subject to coordination with Iranian armed forces, suggesting continued Iranian control and influence," the risk management group Vanguard said. "As such, conditions are likely to remain controlled and potentially restrictive."

Niels Rasmussen, chief analyst for the shipping association Bimco, said "I doubt there will be a large influx of ships" into the Gulf.

"Many ships have already sailed to other regions and they do not want to risk being trapped after the two-week window closes," he said.

- Skies remain restricted -

For the moment, Iraq is the only country in the region to have announced a complete reopening of its airspace.

The United Arab Emirates and Qatar, whose Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Doha hubs handle large quantities of long-haul flights, have maintained many restrictions.

Furthermore, the return to normal jet fuel supplies for the aviation sector will take "several months given the disruptions to refining capacity", warned IATA, the world's leading airline association.

Therefore, "the most immediate lever" for airlines to preserve their operating margins is to "pass on the increased costs to ticket prices".

- Lasting fuel disruptions -

Even with falling oil prices, there will not soon be more physical supply passing through the Strait of Hormuz, given widespread damage to oil and gas infrastructure throughout the Gulf.

"Restarting oilfields and fixing damaged infrastructure is a gradual process, and producers will be cautious about ramping up output without reliable export routes," said Simone Tagliapietra, a fellow at Europe's Bruegel institute.

"Seventy-five energy plants have been attacked and damaged and more than a third of them are seriously or very seriously affected. Recovery will take a long time," Fatih Birol, executive director of the International Energy Agency (IEA), told French daily Le Figaro in an interview published Tuesday.

- Uncertain economic effects -

Stock markets soared and European government borrowing rates plummeted on news of the ceasefire.

"If we quickly return (to February levels), the macroeconomic impact and the impact on budgets won't be very significant, I'd say almost negligible," Claudia Panseri, chief investment officer at UBS Wealth Management France, told AFP.

"If, however, in two weeks, we find ourselves in a situation where there is no agreement, if the price of oil rises back to $100 a barrel, and if gas remains at high levels," the impact on inflation and growth will be more pronounced, Panseri said.

World.title: BAFTA racial slur was breach of BBC editorial standards: internal probe
World.content:
PARIS - The BBC breached its own editorial standards by broadcasting a racial slur during the BAFTA awards ceremony, an internal probe found Wednesday.

The finding follows a "fast-tracked" investigation ordered by former Director-General Tim Davie into the "serious mistake" that saw the racist slur aired during the event in late February.

Tourette's sufferer John Davidson, who inspired one of the winning films, later said he was "deeply mortified" after shouting the N-word at the London film and television awards ceremony, which he said was caused by an "involuntary tic".

According to the investigation report, there was a "lack of clarity" among staff handling the broadcast, which was aired slightly later than the start of the ceremony, about whether the N-word was audible on the recording.

"This resulted in there being a delay before a decision was taken to remove the recording from iPlayer," it said, adding this did not happen until around 9:30am the following day.

"This delay was a serious mistake, because there could be no certainty that the word would be inaudible to all viewers," it added.

The incident was the latest in a string of controversies to hit the BBC.

In June 2025 during the BBC's Glastonbury festival coverage, staff failed to pull a livestream of a performance by Bob Vylan after the punk-rap duo's frontman led the crowds in an anti-Israel chant.

The BBC later apologised and said it would no longer live-broadcast musical performances it deemed to be "high risk".

In another damaging episode, Davie left the BBC last week after resigning in November over the editing of a documentary about US President Donald Trump.

The president has filed a $10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC over the edit for its flagship current affairs programme "Panorama".

Trump alleges the editing of his January 6, 2021 speech made it appear that he had explicitly urged supporters to attack the Capitol, where lawmakers were certifying Democrat Joe Biden's 2020 election victory.

World.title: Ousted: Humphrey Wattanga exits KRA
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Dr Lilian Nyawanda will now serve as the acting Commissioner General at the Kenya Revenue Authority.

Dr Lillian Nyawanda has been appointed acting Commissioner General of the Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) following the exit of Humphrey Wattanga, who has proceeded on terminal leave with immediate effect.

In a statement, the KRA Board of Directors confirmed Wattanga’s departure, bringing to a close his tenure at the helm of the tax authority.

"During his time in office, he was credited with advancing KRA’s mandate and spearheading key organisational restructuring reforms," the statement by the Board's Chair Ndiritu Muriithi read in part.

The Board expressed its appreciation for his service, noting his contribution to strengthening the institution, and wished him success in his future endeavours.

Dr Nyawanda, who currently serves as Commissioner of Customs and Border Control, will take over in an acting capacity as the Board begins the process of recruiting a substantive Commissioner General through a competitive process.

Mulongo was Thursday, August 24, 2023 sworn in as the Commissioner-General of the Kenya Revenue Authority at an event presided over by the Judiciary Chief Registrar Anne Amadi.

Several bodies have reacted to Nyawanda's appointment, terming it critical at a defining moment for revenue administration in the country.

Among them is the Kenya Civilian Revenue Oversight, which has urged Nyawanda and the Board to prioritize and fast-track the rebranding of Kenya Revenue Authority into Kenya Revenue Service.

"This transition is not merely cosmetic; it is strategic and necessary since across the globe, revenue administrations are evolving into service-oriented institutions that emphasize taxpayer engagement, transparency, and voluntary compliance," a statement by the Interim chair, Elijah Girimani, read in part.

World.title: Gachagua unveils DCP candidate for Emurua Dikirr seat, vows to defend Kipsigis community
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP Party leader Rigathi Gachagua hands over a Nomination Certificate to Vincent Kibet Rotich at the Party's head office. [Benard Orwongo, Standard]

DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua has demanded a full and transparent report on the helicopter crash that claimed the life of Emurua Dikirr MP Johanna Ng’eno, insisting that the government must disclose the truth before calling a by-election.

Speaking during the unveiling of the Democratic Citizens Party (DCP) candidate Vincent Kibet Rotich, Gachagua said the circumstances surrounding the crash remain unclear and continue to raise suspicion among residents.

Local leaders and residents have questioned the manner in which Ng’eno’s funeral was conducted, describing it as rushed, especially compared with the delayed burial of the helicopter’s captain.

Many in the constituency believe that critical information was concealed, further fueling calls for an independent, public investigation.

“We are very bitter following that death, we demand answers before anything else. If they won’t provide us with substantive information, then UDA should totally forget about that seat,” said Rotich the DCP candidate.

DCP deputy party leader Cleophas Malala echoed the same sentiments, noting that the people of Dikirr should have been given enough time to mourn their leader.

“We need a full black box report of the plane and all communications before the crash happened,” Malala said.

Gachagua criticised President William Ruto’s administration, accusing it of sidelining the Kipsigis community despite their strong electoral support.

He claimed that government development has bypassed the region and argued that powerful individuals close to the president are being used to suppress Kipsigis political influence.

“I will fight for your rights because Ruto has proven that he cannot fight for you. He is using the likes of Farouk, Murkomen and Sudi to fight the Kipsigis. These are the people he hides behind when targeting leaders who stand with their communities,” Gachagua said.

Gachagua noted that the region deserves a leader who can unapologetically champion its interests, adding that Rotich embodies the values and courage that the late Ng’eno embodied.

“Vincent is our candidate of choice and he has proven that he is capable of standing up to your oppressors,” he said.

The former DP urged Dikirr residents to unite behind the young aspirant.

He stressed that his political conflict is with President Ruto personally and not the Kalenjin community, saying he respects the community that voted overwhelmingly for their joint ticket in 2022.

“Kalenjins are good people; they voted for us, but Ruto decided to kick me out. It is not the Kalenjins that are bad, it is Ruto,” he said.

He said the constituency has a critical opportunity to choose a leader who will restore development and dignity to the region

Rotich will face UDA nominee David Kipsang Keter, who recently won the party’s primaries with 13,749 votes against Bernard Kipkoech Ngeno’s 13,394.

Away from Emurua Dikirr politics, Gachagua also announced that he will hold a political rally in Kikuyu Constituency this Saturday.

He dismissed threats allegedly issued by local MP Kimani Ichung’wah, noting that no part of Kenya is exclusive to any politician.

“I will not be intimidated. Kikuyu constituency is governed by the Constitution, which guarantees freedom of assembly,” he said.

He further accused the MP of attempting to influence police operations and mobilise disruptive groups.

Gachagua assured supporters that security arrangements are underway and that the rally will proceed uninterrupted.
